data.message: Retrieving the official financial statement PDF from the CSE document repository
Document secured and staged for processing
Running multi-dimensional financial health diagnostics with LLM (this may take a minute)...
Health diagnostics finalised for CTC.N0000 — overall score: 86/100 · Good

standardHealthChecks.name: Liquidity Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Current ratio stands at 1.17 and quick ratio at 1.00. Cash and cash equivalents of LKR 28,772 million cover 75.9% of total current liabilities, providing strong short-term liquidity adequacy.

standardHealthChecks.name: Profitability Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Profitability remains exceptionally strong with a Net Profit After Tax margin of 41.7% relative to net revenue (LKR 6,699 million PAT on LKR 16,070 million net revenue) and an annualized ROE exceeding 100%.

standardHealthChecks.name: Debt Management
standardHealthChecks.description: Virtually zero interest-bearing long-term debt, with total lease liabilities of only LKR 128 million against total equity of LKR 12,647 million. Net finance income is positive (LKR 272 million).

standardHealthChecks.name: Cash Flow Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Operating cash flow generated was LKR 2,129 million for the quarter, reduced temporarily by income tax payments of LKR 6,272 million and seasonal working capital movements (trade receivables expansion).

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Excise & Tax Burden Management
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Government levies absorbed 69.1% of turnover (LKR 35,998 million out of LKR 52,068 million turnover), and income tax absorbed 48.5% of PBT. Despite heavy taxation, the company effectively retains high absolute net earnings.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Tobacco manufacturers operate under heavy fiscal regulation where government levies and high corporate income tax rates (45%) significantly dictate top-line conversions to bottom-line profit.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Raw Material & Cost Control Efficiency
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Raw material costs rose to LKR 901 million (vs LKR 478 million in Q1 2025), yet disciplined control over operating expenses (LKR 1,522 million) maintained an operating profit margin (PBT/Net Revenue) of 80.9%.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Operating in volatile macroeconomic conditions requires tight manufacturing cost discipline and supply chain management to maintain high gross and operating margins.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Dividend Sustainability & Capital Return
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Recommended a first interim dividend of LKR 34.00 per share, supported by strong retained earnings of LKR 10,774 million and substantial liquid cash resources.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: As a mature market leader with low capital expenditure requirements (Capex of LKR 38 million vs PAT of LKR 6,699 million), shareholder yield and dividend payout efficiency are primary valuation drivers.

recommendations: Optimize working capital management to mitigate cash lock-up in trade and other receivables, which increased from LKR 5,527 million to LKR 9,249 million during the quarter.
Maintain ongoing cost-savings initiatives to hedge against raw material price volatility and potential future excise duty increases.
Continue active treasury management to maximize returns on short-term cash holdings (LKR 28,772 million) in a fluctuating interest rate environment.
result.analysisNotes: Ceylon Tobacco Company PLC demonstrates stellar financial health characterized by zero long-term bank debt, high profitability margins, robust cash reserves, and exceptional equity returns. The primary risk factors remain external regulatory impacts, such as high taxation rates (45% corporate tax) and potential government levy hikes.
